verses.english: This was said by the Buddha, the Perfected One: that is what I heard.
“Mendicants, meditate observing the ugliness of the body.

verses.pali: ānāpānassati ca vo ajjhattaṁ parimukhaṁ sūpaṭṭhitā hotu;
verses.english: Let mindfulness of breathing be well-established internally on the present.
Meditate observing the impermanence of all conditions.

verses.pali: Asubhānupassīnaṁ, bhikkhave, kāyasmiṁ viharataṁ yo subhāya dhātuyā rāgānusayo so pahīyati.
verses.english: As you meditate observing the ugliness of the body, you will give up desire for the body.

verses.pali: Ānāpānassatiyā ajjhattaṁ parimukhaṁ sūpaṭṭhititāya ye bāhirā vitakkāsayā vighātapakkhikā, te na honti.
verses.english: When mindfulness of breathing is well-established internally on the present, there will be no distressing external thoughts or wishes.

verses.pali: Sabbasaṅkhāresu aniccānupassīnaṁ viharataṁ yā avijjā sā pahīyati, yā vijjā sā uppajjatī”ti.
verses.english: When you meditate observing the impermanence of all conditions, ignorance is given up and knowledge arises.”
and when freed in regards to that,
that peaceful sage, with perfect insight,

verses.pali: Ayampi attho vutto bhagavatā, iti me sutanti.
verses.english: This too is a matter that was spoken by the Blessed One: that is what I heard.
